title: Discover What’s Next: Finding Music, Artists, and Live Events on Tourify
author: Tourify
excerpt: Tourify brings music discovery, artist profiles, local events, and community activity into one connected experience.
hero_image_alt: Audience members holding phones during a live concert performance
body_markdown:
Music discovery rarely happens in only one place. A fan may hear a song in a video, see an artist mentioned by a friend, notice a local event, and then search several different platforms before deciding to listen, follow, or attend. Tourify is designed to connect those moments.

The Tourify discovery experience helps people find artists, music, events, articles, and community activity without separating the live-music world into unrelated apps. Instead of treating a song, an artist profile, and an upcoming show as isolated pieces of information, Tourify connects them so that discovery can lead to a meaningful next step.

## What the discovery feature does

Tourify organizes music and live-event discovery around the people, places, and interests that matter to each user. Fans can explore artists, browse upcoming events, follow accounts, read music and industry coverage, and save opportunities that interest them.

An artist profile can lead to music, videos, tour dates, merchandise, posts, and professional information. An event page can lead to the performers, venue, ticket information, related posts, and other events nearby. This connected structure reduces the amount of searching required to understand what is happening and how to participate.

This matters because music engagement is already spread across many formats and services. IFPI’s *Engaging with Music 2023* study surveyed more than 43,000 people across 26 countries and found that fans use an average of seven different methods to engage with music. A platform that connects discovery with profiles, events, and community activity can help turn fragmented interest into deeper engagement.

## Benefits for fans

For fans, Tourify can make it easier to:

- Discover new artists through music, posts, events, and recommendations.
- Find concerts and music-related experiences based on location and interests.
- Follow artists, venues, organizations, and industry professionals.
- Save events and keep track of upcoming plans.
- Move from discovering an artist to hearing their music or attending a show.
- Read platform-native news, blogs, interviews, and announcements.

The goal is not simply to show more content. It is to make each discovery more useful. When a user finds something interesting, Tourify provides a path toward listening, following, sharing, attending, buying, or connecting.

## Benefits for artists and event organizers

Discovery tools also help creators and organizers become easier to find. A complete artist or event profile gives users more context than a single promotional post.

Artists can connect their music, identity, upcoming events, professional materials, and updates in one place. Venues and organizations can make their calendars, opportunities, and hosted events visible to the people most likely to care about them.

Because these elements are connected, one action can support another. A new music post may lead a listener to an artist profile. That profile may lead to an upcoming show. The show may lead to a ticket purchase, follow, or share.

## How to access discovery tools

1. Sign in to Tourify or create a general user account.
2. Open the main discovery, news, music, or events area from the primary navigation.
3. Add your location and select genres, artists, or interests when those preferences are available.
4. Follow artists, venues, organizations, and people you want to hear from.
5. Save events or add them to your calendar so they are easier to revisit.
6. Open any artist, event, or venue page to explore the related content attached to it.

The more relevant accounts and interests a user follows, the more useful Tourify’s connected discovery experience becomes.

## A more connected music ecosystem

Tourify is built around the idea that music discovery should lead somewhere. A listener should be able to become a fan. A fan should be able to find a show. A show should connect people to the artists, venue, workers, and community behind it.

By bringing those pieces together, Tourify helps make music discovery more actionable for everyone involved.

sources.title: IFPI — Global study finds people are listening to more music in more ways

title: Build a Living EPK: How Tourify Helps Artists Stay Ready for Opportunities
author: Tourify
excerpt: Create a shareable electronic press kit that brings music, media, live data, and booking information together in one professional destination.
hero_image_alt: Laptop showing an analytics dashboard with charts and performance data
body_markdown:
An artist’s electronic press kit should make it easy for a promoter, venue, journalist, buyer, or potential collaborator to understand the project. Too often, however, an EPK becomes a collection of outdated attachments, broken links, old streaming numbers, and multiple versions of the same biography.

Tourify’s EPK and artist-profile tools are designed to replace that scattered process with a living, shareable destination.

## What is a living EPK?

A traditional electronic press kit usually includes an artist biography, music, photos, videos, press coverage, contact information, and performance history. A living EPK includes those essentials while remaining connected to the artist’s current Tourify profile and available data.

Instead of rebuilding a PDF every time something changes, an artist can update the information at its source. A new tour date, featured release, photo, video, or press mention can be reflected in the profile and EPK without sending an entirely new package to every contact.

Berklee Online recommends including an EPK or one-sheet when approaching venues because it gives promoters a practical way to hear the music and review an artist’s performance background. The easier that information is to evaluate, the easier it is for an industry contact to decide whether the artist is a fit.

## What artists can include

A Tourify EPK can organize the most important parts of an artist’s professional identity, including:

- Artist biography and short professional summary.
- Featured songs, releases, and music-player content.
- Photos, videos, and approved promotional media.
- Upcoming and past performance dates.
- Press quotes, coverage, and notable achievements.
- Audience, social, or streaming insights when supported integrations are connected.
- Booking, management, publicity, or general contact information.
- Technical, hospitality, and performance information where applicable.
- Links to tickets, merchandise, websites, and external platforms.

Artists can present this information through a customizable template that matches the visual identity of the project.

## Why connected analytics matter

Streaming and audience analytics help artists understand where listeners are located, which songs are connecting, and how engagement changes over time. Spotify for Artists describes its data as a way to understand who and where an audience is and which songs are connecting most strongly. Apple Music for Artists similarly provides performance information such as plays, listeners, Shazam activity, purchases, and radio spins.

Tourify’s role is to help artists bring useful parts of that broader professional picture into one ecosystem. The goal is not to replace each streaming service’s analytics dashboard. It is to make an artist’s Tourify presence more current, credible, and useful.

## Benefits for artists

A living EPK can help artists:

- Send one professional link instead of several attachments.
- Reduce the risk of sharing outdated information.
- Present music, media, events, and professional details together.
- Create a stronger first impression with promoters and media contacts.
- Maintain different visual styles without rebuilding the underlying content.
- Make booking and press information easier to find.
- Use connected data to support pitches and planning.

The same profile can also serve fans, collaborators, venues, and potential team members, while the EPK view focuses the information for professional use.

## How to access the EPK builder

1. Sign in and select or create an Artist account.
2. Open the Artist Dashboard.
3. Navigate to the profile, appearance, or EPK section.
4. Complete the core artist information, including biography, location, genres, contact details, and featured media.
5. Add music, videos, photos, events, press coverage, and professional documents.
6. Connect supported external services when integrations are available.
7. Select an EPK template and adjust the available appearance settings.
8. Preview the public version on desktop and mobile.
9. Publish the EPK and copy the shareable link.

Before sending the link, confirm that the featured music works, contact information is current, and the strongest material appears first.

## Always ready for the next opportunity

Opportunities often arrive quickly. A venue may need a support act. A journalist may request approved images. A festival buyer may want performance history. A potential manager may want to review audience development.

A living Tourify EPK helps artists respond with a professional, current presentation instead of assembling materials at the last minute. It turns the artist profile into an active business tool—one that grows alongside the career it represents.

sources.title: Berklee Online — How to Book, Plan, and Promote a Live Concert
Spotify for Artists — How to Read Your Spotify for Artists Data
Apple Music for Artists — Music Analytics and Insights

title: From Gig Search to Live Résumé: Tourify’s Jobs and Workforce Ecosystem
author: Tourify
excerpt: Tourify connects job discovery, applications, onboarding, scheduling, and verified work history for the people who make live events happen.
hero_image_alt: Production team working behind the scenes at a live concert control area
body_markdown:
Every live event depends on people whose work may never appear on the marquee. Stagehands, audio engineers, lighting technicians, photographers, runners, security teams, hospitality staff, production managers, drivers, marketers, and many other professionals turn a plan into a real experience.

Tourify’s jobs and workforce ecosystem is designed to connect those workers with opportunities while helping employers manage the complete process—from job posting to onboarding, scheduling, and work history.

## More than a job board

A standard job board usually ends when an application is submitted. Live-event work requires more coordination.

A worker may need to provide certifications, complete forms, accept policies, upload documents, review call times, receive assignments, and communicate with a manager before arriving onsite. Employers may need to compare applicants, approve hires, track onboarding, assign shifts, and confirm that the right people have the right information.

Tourify brings those steps into one connected workflow.

## Tools for workers

General users can present themselves as industry professionals by adding their roles, skills, experience, portfolio material, availability, and other relevant information to their profiles.

Workers can use Tourify to:

- Search for live-event, touring, venue, creative, and production opportunities.
- Apply using an existing professional profile.
- Keep work samples, qualifications, and experience in one place.
- Complete employer-specific onboarding requirements.
- Receive updates about applications, approvals, assignments, and shifts.
- Build a continuing record of completed work through the platform.
- Collect endorsements, badges, or verified experience when supported.

This creates the foundation for a live résumé: a professional history that can develop as a user completes legitimate work through Tourify’s ecosystem.

## Tools for employers

Organizations, venues, artists, and authorized administrators can use workforce tools to:

- Create job listings for specific events, tours, departments, or dates.
- Define required skills, certifications, experience, and availability.
- Review candidates and move them through a structured hiring process.
- Assign the correct onboarding package to each position.
- Track missing forms, documents, and approvals.
- Add hired workers to rosters and teams.
- Schedule shifts, call times, departments, and work zones.
- Maintain a clearer operational record of who is assigned to what.

Structured onboarding is not just paperwork. SHRM’s onboarding guidance emphasizes that quality onboarding supports long-term employee success, productivity, engagement, and retention. In temporary and project-based work, it also helps reduce confusion before the worker arrives.

## The benefits of a connected workflow

For workers, the main benefit is continuity. The information used to apply for a role can remain connected to onboarding, assignments, and completed experience. Users do not need to rebuild their professional identity for every opportunity.

For employers, the benefit is visibility. Hiring status, missing requirements, team assignments, and schedules can be reviewed in a shared system rather than scattered across email threads, spreadsheets, text messages, and paper forms.

A connected workflow can help reduce:

- Duplicate data entry.
- Missed onboarding requirements.
- Confusion about call times or assignments.
- Unclear approval status.
- Incomplete worker records.
- Difficulty confirming prior experience.

## How workers access jobs

1. Create or sign in to a general Tourify account.
2. Complete the professional sections of your profile.
3. Add your industry roles, skills, work history, portfolio, certifications, and availability.
4. Open the Jobs area from the primary navigation.
5. Filter opportunities by role, location, date, organization, or event type.
6. Review the requirements and submit an application.
7. Monitor notifications and application status.
8. Complete any assigned onboarding steps after approval.
9. Review your assignments and schedule once hired.

## How employers access workforce tools

1. Sign in to an eligible Venue, Organization, Artist, or administrative account.
2. Open Jobs, Hiring, Staff, or Workforce from the dashboard.
3. Create a role and connect it to the appropriate event, tour, venue, or organization.
4. Add requirements and select an onboarding template.
5. Publish the opportunity and review applicants.
6. Approve selected candidates and track onboarding completion.
7. Add hired workers to the roster.
8. Create shifts, assignments, and communication updates.

## Building careers through completed work

The live-events industry is highly relationship-driven, but professional relationships become stronger when experience is easier to document and trust.

Tourify’s workforce ecosystem is designed to help people find work, complete the process successfully, and carry the value of that experience forward. Over time, each completed job can contribute to a clearer professional story—one built through real participation in the events and tours that shape the industry.

sources.title: SHRM — Onboarding New Employees: Maximizing Success
SHRM — How to Measure Onboarding Success

title: Run Tours and Events From One Operational Hub
author: Tourify
excerpt: Coordinate dates, teams, logistics, schedules, budgets, files, and communication through a connected Tourify workspace.
hero_image_alt: Music professional operating a laptop and performance equipment during a live event
body_markdown:
A tour is a moving operation. An event is a temporary organization. Both depend on people, schedules, transportation, equipment, money, documents, venues, vendors, and hundreds of decisions that must line up at the right time.

Tourify’s tour and event management tools are designed to give teams one operational home for that work.

## Why centralized operations matter

Live-event planning often begins with a collection of familiar tools: spreadsheets for budgets, calendars for dates, email for approvals, text messages for updates, cloud folders for files, and separate systems for ticketing, staffing, travel, and promotion.

Each tool may be useful on its own, but the information can become difficult to maintain when the project changes. A revised load-in time may need to be updated in several places. A new venue may affect routing, lodging, transportation, staffing, and budget assumptions. An outdated attachment can create a real operational problem.

Project Management Institute describes a tour as a temporary city that must move, build, operate, and tear down repeatedly. That complexity is why shared project information and clear responsibility are essential.

Tourify connects the project around the tour or event itself.

## What teams can manage

Depending on account type and permissions, Tourify can organize:

- Tour and event dates.
- Venue and location information.
- Artist, staff, vendor, and partner assignments.
- Master calendars, daily schedules, and call times.
- Transportation, hotels, flights, and routing.
- Equipment, backline, production, and site requirements.
- Catering, hospitality, and credential information.
- Budgets, expenses, settlements, and financial reporting.
- Contracts, permits, insurance files, riders, and other documents.
- Tasks, notes, approvals, and team communication.
- Jobs, onboarding, rosters, and worker shifts.
- Ticketing, promotion, and event-performance data where enabled.

The goal is not to force every team into a single rigid process. It is to keep the project’s most important information connected so that authorized users can work from the same operational picture.

## Benefits for managers and administrators

A centralized workspace can help managers:

- See the current status of an event or tour.
- Identify missing information before it becomes urgent.
- Assign responsibility instead of relying on informal follow-up.
- Connect a date or venue change to the departments it affects.
- Control access to sensitive files and financial information.
- Compare planned and actual costs.
- Reduce duplicate systems and repeated data entry.
- Maintain a record of decisions and changes.

Role-based access is especially important. A driver may need transportation and call-time details but not full financial reports. A production lead may need equipment and staffing information. An artist may need the itinerary, performance schedule, hospitality details, and approved contacts.

## Benefits for the wider team

Centralized planning is not only for administrators. It gives team members a more reliable way to answer practical questions:

Where do I need to be? When is load-in? Who is my department lead? Which hotel is confirmed? Has the venue approved the latest production requirement? What is still missing?

When information is organized around the project and filtered by role, people spend less time searching for the correct version.

## How to create a tour or event

1. Sign in to an eligible Artist, Venue, Organization, or administrative account.
2. Open the Events, Tours, or Management area of the dashboard.
3. Choose **Create Event** or **Create Tour**.
4. Enter the project name, dates, locations, participants, and core details.
5. Add event dates or tour stops.
6. Invite team members and assign the appropriate permissions.
7. Build the schedule and add tasks, deadlines, files, and notes.
8. Complete the relevant logistics, staffing, budget, and production sections.
9. Review missing information before publishing or advancing the project.
10. Continue updating the workspace as plans change and the project moves into execution.

For a tour, begin with the routing and confirmed dates, then connect each stop to its venue, schedule, travel, lodging, staffing, and financial information. For a single event, begin with the event timeline and responsibility map.

## From planning to execution

Tourify is built to support the complete life of a project—not only the initial announcement.

A tour or event can move from planning to booking, staffing, onboarding, promotion, ticketing, execution, and reporting while retaining the connections between those stages. That continuity creates a stronger operational record and gives teams a better foundation for the next project.

Great live experiences feel effortless to the audience because the work behind them is organized. Tourify helps make that organization visible, connected, and easier to manage.

sources.title: Project Management Institute — Where Projects Meet the Road: On Tour with a PMP
Berklee Online — How to Book, Plan, and Promote a Live Concert

title: Turn Attention Into Revenue With Tourify Marketplace and Promotions
author: Tourify
excerpt: Connect products, services, tickets, merchandise, music, events, and promoted content to the profiles and posts where fans discover them.
body_markdown:
Discovery is valuable, but creators and event professionals also need ways to turn attention into sustainable support.

Tourify’s marketplace and promotions ecosystem is designed to connect what users create or offer with the profiles, posts, events, and audiences already discovering them. Artists can feature merchandise and releases. Professionals can present services. Events can connect people to tickets. Organizations and venues can highlight relevant listings. Eligible users can promote content to expand its reach.

## One storefront connected to a professional identity

A Tourify storefront is not intended to exist separately from the seller’s profile. It is part of the larger professional and community presence.

That means a fan can discover an artist through a song or event, open the artist profile, and find related merchandise or offers. A potential client can discover a photographer’s work, review the portfolio, and open a service listing. A user can see an event post and continue directly toward the event or ticket page.

This reduces the distance between interest and action.

## What users can offer

Tourify’s marketplace model can support several types of listings, including:

- Artist merchandise and physical products.
- Native or externally hosted product listings.
- Creative and professional services.
- Booking, quote, or availability requests.
- Event tickets and related upgrades.
- Music, special releases, or collectible products where enabled.
- Venue, organization, or event-specific offers.
- Shareable listings that can appear in posts and profiles.

External listings can send buyers to an established third-party checkout, while native listings can use Tourify-supported checkout or request workflows when available.

Bandcamp’s Artist Guide emphasizes the importance of direct fan support and notes that merchandise can be a major part of an artist’s sales. Berklee Online similarly recommends developing merchandise that reflects the artist’s identity and the interests of the audience. Tourify extends that direct-to-audience idea by connecting commerce to the broader live-music ecosystem.

## Shareable commerce

A marketplace listing becomes more useful when it can travel through the platform.

Sellers can attach eligible products, services, tickets, or offers to posts. Those posts can be shared, allowing the listing to reach people through discovery and community activity rather than requiring them to find a separate store first.

A strong listing should clearly explain:

- What the buyer receives.
- The price or type of request.
- Fulfillment, delivery, or scheduling expectations.
- Available options, sizes, dates, or quantities.
- Refund, cancellation, or external-checkout terms.
- Who is responsible for the product or service.

Clear information helps users make informed decisions and protects trust between buyers, sellers, and the platform.

## Self-serve promotions

Tourify promotions are designed to let eligible users expand the reach of their own content. Promotable content may include posts, music, events, merchandise, services, announcements, or other approved listings.

A promotion can allow a user to choose an objective, audience, budget, and schedule. Performance reporting can then help the user understand how the promotion delivered.

This gives artists and professionals a path to support specific goals, such as:

- Increasing awareness for a new release.
- Reaching people near an upcoming event.
- Driving attention to tickets or merchandise.
- Promoting a portfolio or service.
- Expanding the reach of an important post.
- Reintroducing successful content to a relevant audience.

Promotions should strengthen useful content, not replace it. A complete profile, clear offer, strong creative asset, and relevant destination all improve the chance that paid reach leads to a meaningful result.

## How to create a marketplace listing

1. Sign in to an eligible account.
2. Open Marketplace, Storefront, Products, Services, or the corresponding profile-management section.
3. Choose the listing type.
4. Add the title, description, images, price or request method, and availability.
5. Select native checkout or add the approved external destination.
6. Add fulfillment, booking, cancellation, and policy details.
7. Preview the public listing.
8. Publish it to the marketplace and your profile.
9. Create a post featuring the listing when appropriate.

## How to promote content

1. Open an eligible post, song, event, product, service, or listing.
2. Select **Promote** or open the Promotions area of the dashboard.
3. Choose the campaign objective.
4. Select the audience, location, interests, or other available targeting.
5. Set the budget and campaign dates.
6. Review the destination and preview the promoted content.
7. Submit the campaign for approval and payment.
8. Monitor delivery and results from the promotions dashboard.

Feature access may depend on account eligibility and the current Tourify rollout.

## Building a healthier creator economy

Tourify’s marketplace and promotions ecosystem is designed around a simple idea: the people creating value in music and live events should have clearer ways to connect that value to an audience.

By linking commerce and promotion to trusted profiles, events, posts, and professional history, Tourify can help creators earn support without separating business activity from the community and work that made the audience care in the first place.

sources.title: Berklee Online — How to Create Music Merch to Grow Your Brand
U.S. Small Business Administration — E-Commerce and Digital Opportunities
